text.p: Mexican media company Grupo Televisa on Thursday said it was confident a new push on programming would pay dividends in audience share, which it has steadily lost in recent years to upstart rival TV Azteca.

Two new soap operas that start in early August and a revamped 24 Horas nightly news program should recoup market share for Televisa during key prime-time hours, said company head of programming Jaime Davila.

"We have an important challenge in the time period from 9 p.m. to midnight, when our market share is about 68.2 percent," Davila told analysts during a conference call following Televisa's second quarter results.
"But that is exactly where we have prepared our attack," he said.

TV Azteca's popular prime-time program Ciudad Desnuda had lost about 43 percent from its peak earlier this year -- when it obtained a nearly 19 points household rating, meaning nearly one out of every five television homes were tuned in.
Televisa juggled its programming to couter the tabloid news-magazine show, which features stories about everything from crime to witchcraft.
"We have reconquered, then, the most strategic part of television time and taken away from our rivals their launching pad for boosting ratings in other hours," Davila said.
It is difficult to measure exact audience market share for both companies because each company measures their prime-time hours differently.
Analysts estimate that Televisa has about 68 percent market share during prime-time versus 29 percent for TV Azteca. Only a few years ago, Televisa's audience share was above 80 percent.
While Televisa is more dominant in the early hours of the day, Azteca has made a successful push at night.
"From 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. we have exceeded our goals, acheiving the highest levels of market share since we began measuring last year," Davila said.
Davila said Televisa's direct-to-home (DTH) satellite TV venture with News Corp had signed up about 60,000 subscribers -- putting it ahead of its year-end goal of 95,000, he said.
